name: Abū Mūsā ʿĪsā ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Jazūlī
summary: Berber grammarian of the Maghrib whose al-Muqaddima al-Jazūliyya, a short and famously hard book of naḥw, was commented on by the masters of al-Andalus.
bio: Al-Jazūlī came from the Berber Jazūla of southern Morocco, studied in Cairo with Ibn Barrī, and taught in the Maghrib. His al-Muqaddima, also called al-Qānūn, grew out of notes on his teacher's lessons; it is so compressed that the sources say many who read it could not follow it, and it called forth commentaries by al-Shalawbīn, Ibn ʿUṣfūr and others. He died in the Maghrib around 607/1210.
uncertain: His year of death is given as 607, 610 or 616 (1210–1219).
